subject: Private deployment: License vs support subsidy — special-case request
messages:
From: Eli Rosen <eli.rosen@clearstream.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clearstream.com
Date: Tue, 05 May 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment pricing question — license v. support subsidy

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the performance and the SLOs you showed. Procurement asked me to get clarity on two items before we take the SOW to legal:

1) Our capital plan prefers to capitalize license-like items rather than OPEX (platform fee). Is there a path to convert a portion of the platform fee into a license or amortized operator license so we can meet our accounting constraints?
2) If conversion isn’t feasible, would Redwood consider a one-time support subsidy (credit against platform fee) tied to a 24-month commitment? We have a hard budget ceiling in year 1 and that subsidy would make the economics work.

Can you share a draft SOW and a pricing matrix that shows both options? We’d like to review internally and give you a greenlight next week if the numbers line up.

Appreciate it —
Eli Rosen
Director of Cloud Ops, Clearstream
eli.rosen@clearstream.com
+1 415-555-0123
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Eli Rosen <eli.rosen@clearstream.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 05 May 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment pricing question — license v. support subsidy

Hi Eli —

Really glad the demo resonated. Short answers up front and I’ve looped in Marissa and Ben for commercial/legal/ops alignment:

- License conversion: We can offer an operator-license amortization option for a subset of the stack (operator/runtime licenses) that customers can capitalize; it requires a 24-month minimum term and has a different invoice cadence. Not all platform-fee revenue is eligible.
- Support subsidy: We can approve a one-time subsidy against the platform fee in year 1 for qualified deals, subject to approval (commercial + finance) and linkage to a committed usage term.

I’m attaching a SOW draft and a pricing matrix showing three scenarios: (A) platform-fee only, (B) platform-fee with a year-1 subsidy, and (C) hybrid with operator-license amortization + reduced platform-fee.

Internal ask: Marissa / Ben — can you confirm what range of one-time subsidy we can approve for a mid-market account w/ 24-month commit? Also need input on whether we should require an SLA carveout/addendum for subsidized deals.

Eli, I’ll follow up with proposed numbers by tomorrow.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 05 May 2026 13:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment pricing question — license v. support subsidy

Stephanie / Ben —

Thanks for the context. High level: we can make concessions for strategic mid-market accounts but need guardrails so we don’t set a precedent that erodes floor economics. Proposed guardrails:

- Subsidy approach (preferred): one-time credit against platform fee in year 1 equal to 15% of year-1 platform fee, capped at $200k. Requires a 24-month committed usage (minimum). Finance will require the subsidy to be recognized over the commitment term for accounting.
- Amortization approach: allow capitalization by converting up to 40% of year-1 platform fee into operator licenses that can be invoiced as capital (amortized). This reduces recognized ARR but preserves gross margin on installed operator licenses.
- SLA carveout: for subsidized deals, legal wants a standard addendum limiting on-call SRE commitments to a defined retainer band (we can offer bronze/silver/gold retainer options). No unlimited on-call.

If Eli is flexible on the 24-month lock we can soften caps, but prefer firm commitable term. Approve headline numbers above for Steph to propose to the customer.

Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 06 May 2026 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment pricing question — license v. support subsidy

Quick operational note: if we go the subsidy plus amortization hybrid we need to map support tiers to response windows in the SOW. Suggested mapping (I can attach as a csv):
- Bronze: 8x5 email + 48hr P1 SLA window + access to knowledge base
- Silver: 24x7 email + 8hr P1 + 1x monthly incident review
- Gold: 24x7 phone + 4hr P1 + named SRE on retainer

For Clearstream, recommend Silver as default for the subsidized option; Gold only if they also buy the on-call retainer. I updated the support_sla_table.csv with pricing deltas and will attach to the SOW package.

Ben Carter
Solutions Director, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, procurement@clearstream.com
Date: Fri, 07 May 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment pricing question — license v. support subsidy

Eli —

Appreciate the patience while we aligned internally. Attached are the SOW_draft_v1.pdf and pricing_matrix.xlsx (plus support_sla_table.csv) for your review. Summary of the approved special-case options we can offer to Clearstream:

1) Subsidy path (recommended): 15% credit against year-1 platform fee, capped at $200,000. Condition: 24-month term commitment and signed SOW. Credit applied as one invoice credit in month 2, recognized over the 24-month term for revenue accounting.
2) Amortization path: convert up to 40% of year-1 platform fee into operator licenses that Clearstream can capitalize. Requires separate license schedule; invoice cadence can be adjusted to support capitalization.
3) Support mapping: default to Silver support for the subsidized scenario (24x7 email + 8hr P1). Gold on-call retainer is available as an add-on per the attached table.

Next steps we recommend:
- You review the SOW/Pricing and confirm which path you prefer.
- If subsidy route: sign SOW and return by 2026-05-20 to lock the cap.
- If amortization route: procurement/legal to confirm capitalization requirements and we’ll loop in finance to produce the license schedule.
